core.headline: Victorian end-of-terrace cottage in Smarden Conservation Area
core.summary: A red-brick cottage dating from c.1880, set in the heart of Smarden village. The accommodation retains its cast-iron fireplace, ledged-and-braced doors and quarry-tiled kitchen floor, with a cottage garden behind.
core.listing:
Number 2 Forge Cottages stands at the end of a Victorian terrace on The Street in Smarden, a village within the Ashford Borough Conservation Area. Built around 1880 of red brick under a clay-tiled roof, the cottage offers two-bedroom accommodation with a cast-iron fireplace, ledged-and-braced doors and a quarry-tiled kitchen floor.

The front door opens into the sitting room, which measures 3.90m x 3.60m (12'10" x 11'10") and has a cast-iron fireplace. Beyond lies the kitchen/dining room, 4.30m x 3.20m (14'1" x 10'6"), with a quarry-tiled floor and a range alcove; the exposed beams here are reclaimed, installed in the 1990s. Upstairs, bedroom one measures 3.80m x 3.30m (12'6" x 10'10") and bedroom two 2.90m x 2.40m (9'6" x 7'10"), served by a bathroom. There is restricted head height at the top of the stairs, approximately 1.88m (6'2").

The rear cottage garden extends approximately 12m (40ft), laid with a brick path and served by a timber shed.

Smarden village has a pub approximately two minutes' walk away.

Guide Price £425,000. Freehold. Council Tax Band C (Ashford Borough Council). EPC rating E. The property is of standard construction: red brick under a clay-tiled roof. Electricity and water are mains connected (water not metered). Sewerage is to a septic tank, shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance apply and emptying costs are shared. Heating is oil-fired central heating. Broadband: FTTC. Mobile signal: good outdoors, variable indoors. Parking: on-street. Building safety: none known. The property lies within the Smarden Conservation Area. The rear of the garden is in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded. Coastal erosion: none known. Planning: none known. Accessibility: none known. Coalfield/mining: none known. The seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. There is restricted head height at the top of the stairs, approximately 1.88m (6'2"). Chain involved.

fixes: Add EMAIL BLAST: 3 subject lines (≤60 chars each), preview (≤90 chars), and email body (2–4 paragraphs ending with material-information line)
Add SELLER APPROVAL EMAIL: 150–250 words summarising the property for the vendor
Add SOCIAL: 3 distinct social media posts as required by format specification

Strengthen voice fit: current copy is factual/neutral, not 'warm, cinematic, story-led' Heritage voice. Open with evocative scene-setting (e.g. 'The brick path winds past...' or 'Light falls through...')
Headline could lead with story/character: consider 'A Victorian cottage on The Street' or similar to match Heritage voice
Portal description: weave narrative thread through rooms rather than inventory format to match cinematic brief
Strapline: add warmth/story element beyond pure facts (e.g. reference village life, the forge history, or sensory detail)
Key features: rephrase to avoid list format where possible, integrate story elements
